scope: Proposition 6.1 of the manuscript “A power saving for planar halving lines” (preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-halving-lines-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 183 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 61d7aa1ffad4b796), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a Borel set G ⊂ E with λK0 (G) > 0, a further subsequence, and a translation and uniform rescaling of each normalized Euclidean plane with the following properties. Over every p ∈ π(G) the limiting graph of the maps Ln has a unique position l(p) in the closed unit disk. With η = 1/16, there is cG > 0 such that |l(p) − l(q)| ≥ cG|p − q|1+η (p, q ∈ π(G)). (6.2) Attach Euclidean position as an additional compactified coordinate to the vertex measures, and take a weak limit e µ. Its restriction by the old-label condition z ∈ G has position marginal νG satisfying νG(B(x, r)) ≤ CGrd∗ , d∗ = 2 1 + η = 32 17 , x ∈ R2 , 0 < r < 1. (6.3) Consequently every strip of width r has νG-mass at most C′ Grd∗−1, uniformly in its position and direction. Every line has zero νG-mass.
